\chapter{Taking a stand}
\label{ch:ar-taking-a-stand}
\hlchaptermodality{373}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone took sides, held on, gave way, backed down or settled a question.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 373: I can say that someone took sides, held on, gave way, backed down or settled a question.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انحاز} (inḥāza)}{انحاز (inḥāza)}]{\ar{انحاز} (inḥāza) — to take sides}

\label{lesson:AR-C373-inhaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to fall short, then the Arabic for to manage to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انحاز}}
\textbf{\ar{انحاز}} — \emph{inḥāza} — \textquotedblleft{}to take sides\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انحاز} \ar{الحكم} \ar{إلى} \ar{الفريق} \ar{الآخر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inḥāza al-ḥakam ilā al-farīq al-ākhar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The referee took the side of the other team.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينحاز}, \emph{yanḥāz}.

It takes \ar{إلى}: \ar{انحاز} \ar{إلى} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انحاز}} (\emph{inḥāza}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw together, to gather\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VII, to draw oneself aside to one party: to take sides.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inḥāza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inḥāza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inḥāza al-ḥakam ilā al-farīq al-ākhar.} — The referee took the side of the other team.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to fall short, then the Arabic for to manage to, then say \emph{inḥāza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{انحاز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To take sides\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تمسك} (tamassaka)}{تمسك (tamassaka)}]{\ar{تمسك} (tamassaka) — to hold on to}

\label{lesson:AR-C373-tamassaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to manage to, then the Arabic for to take sides.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تمسك}}
\textbf{\ar{تمسك}} — \emph{tamassaka} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold on to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تمسك} \ar{الرجل} \ar{برأيه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tamassaka ar-rajul bi-raʾyih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man held on to his opinion.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتمسك}, \emph{yatamassak}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{تمسك} \ar{بـ} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تمسك}} (\emph{tamassaka}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-s-k}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold, to grasp\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to keep a firm hold: to cling to a thing. \ar{أمسك}, to hold, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamassaka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamassaka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tamassaka ar-rajul bi-raʾyih.} — The man held on to his opinion.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to manage to, then the Arabic for to take sides, then say \emph{tamassaka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تمسك} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hold on to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تنازل} (tanāzala)}{تنازل (tanāzala)}]{\ar{تنازل} (tanāzala) — to concede; to give up}

\label{lesson:AR-C373-tanazala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to take sides, then the Arabic for to hold on to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تنازل}}
\textbf{\ar{تنازل}} — \emph{tanāzala} — \textquotedblleft{}to concede; to give up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تنازل} \ar{الأخ} \ar{عن} \ar{حقه} \ar{في} \ar{البيت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tanāzala al-akh ʿan ḥaqqihi fī al-bayt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The brother gave up his right to the house.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتنازل}, \emph{yatanāzal}.

It takes \ar{عن}: \ar{تنازل} \ar{عن} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تنازل}} (\emph{tanāzala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-z-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to come down, to descend\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, to come down from a claim: to concede, to give a thing up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanāzala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanāzala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tanāzala al-akh ʿan ḥaqqihi fī al-bayt.} — The brother gave up his right to the house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to take sides, then the Arabic for to hold on to, then say \emph{tanāzala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تنازل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To concede; to give up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تراجع} (tarājaʿa)}{تراجع (tarājaʿa)}]{\ar{تراجع} (tarājaʿa) — to back down}

\label{lesson:AR-C373-tarajaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to hold on to, then the Arabic for to concede.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تراجع}}
\textbf{\ar{تراجع}} — \emph{tarājaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to back down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تراجع} \ar{أبي} \ar{عن} \ar{قراره} \ar{بعد} \ar{نقاش}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tarājaʿa abī ʿan qarārihi baʿda niqāsh.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father backed down from his decision after a discussion.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتراجع}, \emph{yatarājaʿ}.

It takes \ar{عن}: \ar{تراجع} \ar{عن} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تراجع}} (\emph{tarājaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to return, to go back\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VI, to go back step by step: to back down, to decline.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarājaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarājaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarājaʿa abī ʿan qarārihi baʿda niqāsh.} — My father backed down from his decision after a discussion.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to hold on to, then the Arabic for to concede, then say \emph{tarājaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تراجع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To back down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حسم} (ḥasama)}{حسم (ḥasama)}]{\ar{حسم} (ḥasama) — to resolve; to settle}

\label{lesson:AR-C373-hasama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to concede, then the Arabic for to back down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حسم}}
\textbf{\ar{حسم}} — \emph{ḥasama} — \textquotedblleft{}to resolve; to settle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حسم} \ar{المدير} \ar{المسألة} \ar{في} \ar{يوم} \ar{واحد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥasama al-mudīr al-masʾala fī yawm wāḥid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager settled the matter in a single day.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحسم}, \emph{yaḥsim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حسم}} (\emph{ḥasama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-s-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to cut off\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ḥasama} is a Form I verb: to cut a question off, to settle it for good.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥasama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥasama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥasama al-mudīr al-masʾala fī yawm wāḥid.} — The manager settled the matter in a single day.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to concede, then the Arabic for to back down, then say \emph{ḥasama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حسم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To resolve; to settle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 366–373 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R373-review-366-373}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for to claim and to allege.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to claim, to allege, to cast doubt, to believe someone, to infer
  \item to realize, to conceive, to grasp, awareness, knowledge
  \item importance, a value, to focus, to neglect, to care about
  \item to advise, to hint, to encourage, to hesitate, an alternative
  \item to criticize, to oppose, to justify, to exaggerate, to generalize
  \item a means, to strive, to accomplish, to contribute, an incentive
  \item an obstacle, a difficulty, a dilemma, to fall short, to manage to
  \item to take sides, to hold on to, to concede, to back down, to resolve
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To claim? (\textbf{\ar{ادعى}}, \emph{iddaʿā}.) To allege? (\textbf{\ar{زعم}}, \emph{zaʿama}.) To cast doubt? (\textbf{\ar{شكك}}, \emph{shakkaka}.) To believe someone? (\textbf{\ar{صدق}}, \emph{ṣaddaqa}.) To infer? (\textbf{\ar{استدل}}, \emph{istadalla}.) To realize? (\textbf{\ar{أدرك}}, \emph{adraka}.) To conceive? (\textbf{\ar{تصور}}, \emph{taṣawwara}.) To grasp? (\textbf{\ar{استوعب}}, \emph{istawʿaba}.) Awareness? (\textbf{\ar{وعي}}, \emph{waʿy}.) Knowledge? (\textbf{\ar{معرفة}}, \emph{maʿrifa}.) Importance? (\textbf{\ar{أهمية}}, \emph{ahammiyya}.) A value? (\textbf{\ar{قيمة}}, \emph{qīma}.) To focus? (\textbf{\ar{ركز}}, \emph{rakkaza}.) To neglect? (\textbf{\ar{أهمل}}, \emph{ahmala}.) To care about? (\textbf{\ar{اهتم}}, \emph{ihtamma}.) To advise? (\textbf{\ar{نصح}}, \emph{naṣaḥa}.) To hint? (\textbf{\ar{لمح}}, \emph{lammaḥa}.) To encourage? (\textbf{\ar{شجع}}, \emph{shajjaʿa}.) To hesitate? (\textbf{\ar{تردد}}, \emph{taraddada}.) An alternative? (\textbf{\ar{بديل}}, \emph{badīl}.) To criticize? (\textbf{\ar{انتقد}}, \emph{intaqada}.) To oppose? (\textbf{\ar{عارض}}, \emph{ʿāraḍa}.) To justify? (\textbf{\ar{برر}}, \emph{barrara}.) To exaggerate? (\textbf{\ar{بالغ}}, \emph{bālagha}.) To generalize? (\textbf{\ar{عمم}}, \emph{ʿammama}.) A means? (\textbf{\ar{وسيلة}}, \emph{wasīla}.) To strive? (\textbf{\ar{سعى}}, \emph{saʿā}.) To accomplish? (\textbf{\ar{أنجز}}, \emph{anjaza}.) To contribute? (\textbf{\ar{ساهم}}, \emph{sāhama}.) An incentive? (\textbf{\ar{حافز}}, \emph{ḥāfiz}.) An obstacle? (\textbf{\ar{عقبة}}, \emph{ʿaqaba}.) A difficulty? (\textbf{\ar{صعوبة}}, \emph{ṣuʿūba}.) A dilemma? (\textbf{\ar{معضلة}}, \emph{muʿḍila}.) To fall short? (\textbf{\ar{أخفق}}, \emph{akhfaqa}.) To manage to? (\textbf{\ar{تمكن}}, \emph{tamakkana}.) To take sides? (\textbf{\ar{انحاز}}, \emph{inḥāza}.) To hold on to? (\textbf{\ar{تمسك}}, \emph{tamassaka}.) To concede? (\textbf{\ar{تنازل}}, \emph{tanāzala}.) To back down? (\textbf{\ar{تراجع}}, \emph{tarājaʿa}.) To resolve? (\textbf{\ar{حسم}}, \emph{ḥasama}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
